finding.claim: Unauthenticated insecure deserialization: attacker-supplied base64 `state` param is passed to Marshal.load, enabling arbitrary object instantiation and remote code execution via Ruby gadget chains.

trace.note: Base64.decode64(params[:state]) yields raw bytes passed directly to Marshal.load
deserialized object is inspected and returned

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, authorization, class allowlist, or signature/HMAC on the payload; no before filters or middleware in app.rb. Sinatra's built-in protections do not cover Marshal.load of untrusted input.

verdict.reason: app.rb:5-6 shows the unauthenticated POST /restore route passing Base64.decode64(params[:state]) straight into Marshal.load, with no auth, filter, allowlist or signature anywhere in the file (app.rb is the only source file), so an anonymous attacker can trigger unsafe deserialization.

verdict_facts.reason: app.rb:5-6 shows POST /restore passing Base64.decode64(params[:state]) straight into Marshal.load with no auth, before filter, allowlist or HMAC, so any HTTP client can feed it a malicious Marshal payload.
